problem: Existing open-vocabulary mobile manipulation and multimodal retrieval methods (CLIP, BEiT-3, HomeRobot, Embodied-RAG) rely on flat similarity or LLM node selection, confuse visually similar but semantically wrong candidates, and ignore whether the retrieved object or receptacle is actually manipulable, which causes execution failures.
motivation: Service robots operate repeatedly in known buildings with hundreds of pre-explored images, so exhaustive VLM scoring of every view is impractical. When several valid candidates exist, the robot should pick the one that is easiest to grasp or place on (upright, uncluttered), which requires affordance-aware memory and reranking.
key_idea: Build a hierarchical affordance-aware embodied memory (affordance, instance, view, zone, area, building) from pre-explored images, then retrieve top-down with fused regional (text) and visual semantics and rerank with VLM-predicted pick/place affordance scores.
insight: Regional and visual semantics are complementary. Removing either drops overall R@10 from 37.1 to 32.1 (no regional) or 30.0 (no visual), and the alpha sweep degrades when biased to either side. Reranking with structured instance/affordance nodes is worth 7.6 R@10 points over no reranking, and beats caption-only LLM reranking by 5.9 points. In the real world, affordance score reranking (ASR) raises SR from 70% to 85% at identical R@5 (94), so suitability matters beyond semantic correctness.
method: Affordance Proposer (levels 1-2): SEEM masks are overlaid with numbered visual prompts and fed with the original image to a VLM (GPT-4o), which outputs instance-affordance-score triplets (descriptive instance, pick/place, score).
Multi-Level Representation (level 3): each view stores a regional semantic embedding (text-embedding-3-large of the VLM image description) and a visual embedding (BEiT-3 image encoder).
Area Summarizer (levels 4..N): recursive agglomerative clustering by Euclidean position and description-embedding cosine similarity, with an LLM summary per cluster embedded as the higher-level node.
Recursive Top-Down Traversal: from level N to 3, select top-K_b nodes per level by cosine similarity between the instruction text embedding and node text embeddings (precomputed, no LLM selection).
Multi-Level Fusion: view score = alpha*sim(text, regional emb) + (1-alpha)*sim(BEiT-3 text feature, visual emb).

Affordance-Aware Reranking: for the top-K_r views, prefilter instances by pick (object) or place (receptacle), have an LLM score descriptions against the instruction, rerank the top-K_f by affordance score (ASR), then reorder views by their selected instances.

setting.observation: RGB images from pre-exploration (6 panoramic views per waypoint in sim; a single fixed-viewpoint RGB in real world, RealSense D435i); depth used for grasp point in real world
setting.action_space: retrieval outputs ranked images; execution uses heuristic navigation and grasp/place to the location of the user-selected image
setting.simulator: Matterport3D (image collection only, retrieval benchmark); real-world Stretch 2
setting.privileged: pre-exploration images of the environment (map used to choose waypoints in MP3D); no GT semantics at test time

numbers.extra: Uses pre-explored images (avg 590 per environment); ASR excluded because no physical execution

results: On the new WholeHouse-MM benchmark, Affordance RAG reaches overall R@10 of 37.1 versus 28.7 for the best baseline (BEiT-3), and beats all baselines on every recall metric. In real-world tests it reaches 85% SR versus 45% for BEiT-3 and 70% without ASR.
limitations: Assumes all relevant visual information is covered by pre-explored images, which fails under heavy occlusion; there is no active exploration.
Considers only visual and spatial affordances and no physical or kinematic constraints; real-world grasping and navigation use heuristics.
The real-world evaluation is small (40 trials, one room), and the benchmark evaluates retrieval only, with low absolute receptacle recall and SR@K.
